full_judgment:
2. The petitioner as plaintiff in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 836 of 1998 instituted Title Suit No. 222 of 1992 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Chandpur for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession against the respondents on the allegations inter alia that he is the owner of the suit property. The respondent No. 1 filed Title Suit No. 93 of 1985 for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession on the selfsame ground of ownership. 

 3. The area of suit land is 1/2 decimal of land with a shop on the same and both the parties claim ownership over the same. Md Saifullah, respondent No. 1 in both the appeals instituted Title Suit No. 93 of 1985 (defendant of the Title Suit No. 222 of 1992) has claimed that the property appertained to CS Plot No. 313, while Moulana Serajul Haque plaintiff in Title Suit No. 222 of 1992 has claimed that the suit land appertained to CS Plot No. 312. Both the suits were for declaration of title and for recovery of khas possession. 

 7. The findings of the High Court Division are that the present Title Suit No. 222 of 1992 filed by the same plaintiff of Title Suit No. 90 of 1986 is barred by resjudicata as the subsequent suit was filed for the selfsame land. It may be stated that the Title Suit No. 90 of 1986 was filed for declaration of title, confirmation of possession and for permanent injunction in respect of ½ decimal of land of plot No. 312. Title Suit No. 45 of 1991 subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No. 222 of 1992 was filed for recovery of khas possession as in the meantime the plaintiff was dispossessed as claimed by him. So, we are unable to agree with the findings of the High Court Division that the subsequent suit was barred by resjudicata. We are also of the view that Title Suit No. 222 of 1992 having been filed within 12 years from the date of dispossession the suit was quite maintainable as the title of Moulana Serajul Haque was earlier declared by a competent court in Title Suit No. 90 of 1986 and the decree was upheld up to the appellate stage and the decree stands still valid.
